LESSON: NATIONAL UNITY IN KENYA -NATIONAL SYMBOLS -NATIONAL DAYS -NATIONAL LANGUAGES

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade five
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Governance
Topic 5.1: National Unity in Kenya -National Symbols -National Days -National languages
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers National Unity in Kenya -National Symbols -National Days -National languages, part of Governance in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade five SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How can we promote National unity in our country?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on National Unity in Kenya -National Symbols -National Days -National languages together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Citizenship: Learners understand the impact of a person's rights and responsibilities in society as they brainstorm in groups factors which

promote national unity in Kenya (National Symbols, National Days and National languages).

● Creativity and Imagination: Learners undertake tasks that encourage artistic expression of ideas as they draw and colour the national

symbols in Kenya using the locally available materials. (The Coat of arms. The national flag and the Public Seal).

Values:
• Patriotism: learners love their own country as they Sing and write down in groups, the three stanzas of the National anthem of Kenya.

• Unity: Learners display team spirit as think pair and share national symbols in Kenya. (The Coat of arms. The national flag, the national

anthem and the Public Seal).

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
• Human Rights and Responsibilities: Learners enhance cohesiveness as they brainstorm in groups factors which promote national unity in

Kenya (National Symbols, National Days and National languages).

• Patriotism and Good Governance: Learners demonstrate patriotism as they sing and write down in groups, the three stanzas of the National

anthem of Kenya.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:


Remember the key question: How can we promote National unity in our country?
